when: lane phase, their marksman or their support is dead and their bot outer tower is up
asks: they're dead do I hit tower
plates or recall
should I take plates or back
do I stay for plates
one of them died what now
say: Shove this wave in and take plates while they're dead, or recall now if your gold finishes an item before they're back.
more: A dead laner can't defend plate gold, and a wave dying at their tower also costs them minions on the walk back.
Recalling instead means you return with an item they don't have, and that item is what wins the next two-on-two.
Either way, be gone before the respawn timer ends. One wave too many is how their jungler finds you low and far up the lane.
check: Where their jungler was last seen, and how big the wave you are pushing is.
breaks: If their jungler is unseen and you are both low, skip the plates: shove once and recall.

when: lane phase, nobody in bot lane is dead and you lead their marksman in CS
asks: can I hit the tower
is it safe to take a plate
should I push for plates
do I go for tower now
say: Take a plate only with the wave under their tower and their jungler seen elsewhere, or hold the wave mid-lane and keep farming if he's missing.
more: Plates are worth a lot, but hitting a tower puts you at the far end of a long lane with both enemies alive.
A sighting of their jungler on the other side is a short window. It runs out as fast as he can walk back.
If you keep the farm lead instead, the tower falls later anyway once your item gap is real.
check: Whether their jungler has shown on the map in the last few seconds, and whether your river brush is warded.
breaks: If their jungler has not been seen for a while, treat him as nearby: stop at the middle of the lane and farm.
basis: pro:A jungler seen on the far side opens yours

when: your team destroyed their bot outer tower and their mid outer tower still stands
asks: we got bot tower now what
do I stay bot after tower
should I go mid now
where do I go after first tower
tower's down where next
say: Move to mid with your support and take that tower next, or stay bot one more wave if a dragon spawns there within a minute.
more: Mid is the short lane, so a fragile carry is never far from a tower, and you can reach either river first.
A solo laner who can survive alone is better suited to the long bot lane you just opened.
Their mid outer tower guards both river entrances. Once it falls, their team has to walk blind to every dragon.
check: Whether your mid laner is moving to a side lane, and how soon the next dragon is up.
breaks: If your mid laner will not swap, farm bot only as far as the river and walk mid when an objective is close.

when: a dragon is up or spawns within a minute and nobody near bot is dead
asks: dragon's coming what do I do
do I go to dragon
should I leave lane for drake
dragon soon do I push
are we doing dragon
say: Push your wave now and walk to river with your support before it spawns, or stay and farm if your jungler isn't coming.
more: The lane that shoves first gets to the river first. Arriving second means walking in through brushes you can't see into.
Pushing costs you nothing if the fight never happens, because the wave dies at their tower while you are away.
If your jungler is on the other side of the map, the dragon isn't yours to take. Keep the farm instead of posturing.
check: Where your jungler is, and whether your wave can actually be pushed in before the spawn.
breaks: If their duo has the wave pushed into you, don't abandon it to arrive late. Clear it under tower and give the dragon.
basis: pro:The lane that pushes first moves first

when: a dragon is up and your support is dead
asks: my support's dead do I go dragon
should I help drake alone
support died can we still do dragon
do I rotate without my support
say: Stay under tower and farm until your support is back, or join the dragon late from behind your team if they've already started it.
more: Their duo is two players against your one, so they reach the river first and you would be walking into them alone.
What matters is how many bodies each side can bring, and right now your side is short one.
If your team commits anyway, come in behind them from your own jungle rather than through the river.
check: How many enemies are showing near the pit, and whether your team has actually started the dragon.
breaks: If their bot lane is also down a player, the numbers are even again and you can walk over with the wave pushed.
basis: pro:Count who can actually arrive before contesting

when: their jungler is dead with a respawn timer running and a dragon is up
asks: their jungler died do we take dragon
jungler's dead what do we do
free dragon?
should we go drake now
enemy jungle is dead
say: Their jungler's dead, so drop the lane and help burn dragon right now, or take tower plates if your jungler is too far away.
more: Without Smite on their side there is no reliable steal, so the only question is whether you kill it before he respawns.
Your damage is what makes it fast. A marksman on the dragon shortens the take more than anyone else.
If your own jungler can't get there, use the same window on the tower. Their team is a player short either way.
check: Whether your jungler is close enough to arrive, and whether the respawn timer outlasts the take.
breaks: If their timer is nearly up and the dragon is still healthy, back off rather than hand him a Smite fight.
basis: pro:A dead jungler makes the objective free

when: their marksman has more completed items than you and the enemy team has fewer than three dragons
asks: do we fight this dragon
I'm behind should I go drake
can we contest dragon
should we give this one
say: Let this dragon go and collect the bot and mid waves for your item, or show up only if their marksman is dead.
more: A dragon fight is decided by finished items. One item behind on the main damage dealers usually means losing the fight and the dragon.
An early dragon you give up costs far less than a lost fight that also gives them towers.
The waves you take meanwhile close the item gap, so the next dragon is fought on even terms.
check: How far you are from finishing your item, and how many dragons they already have.
breaks: If this would be their third dragon, the next one is soul. Plan to fight that one with everybody there.
basis: pro:Do not fight an objective one spike behind

when: the enemy team has killed three dragons and the next one spawns within two minutes
asks: they're on soul point what do we do
do we have to fight this dragon
they get soul next
how do we stop soul
say: This dragon gives them soul, so recall early and arrive with your team, or trade for Baron if it's past twenty minutes and you can't fight.
more: Four dragons give the soul, a permanent team-wide buff. This is the one dragon you cannot keep giving away.
Recall a full minute early so you walk in with your gold spent and your team around you.
If the fight is truly unwinnable, take the biggest thing on the other side of the map at the same moment.
check: Whether your team is grouping, and whether Baron is alive and reachable.
breaks: If two of your teammates are dead when it spawns, don't walk in. Defend towers and look for a pick after they take it.
basis: pro:Give early dragons, then fight the one before soul point

when: your team has killed three dragons
asks: we're on soul point how do we set up
one more dragon what do I do
how do we get soul
soul dragon is next
say: Recall, spend your gold and walk to dragon as five a minute early, or push mid first if they refuse to leave base.
more: You only need to not lose this fight. Arriving first with items bought makes them walk into you.
Gold sitting unspent is not a lead. Buy before the spawn, not after.
A pushed mid wave means they lose a tower if all five of them come to the pit.
check: How much gold you are holding, and where the mid wave is.
breaks: If their jungler is alive and yours is dead, don't start it. Hold the area and wait for your jungler.
basis: pro:A lead is not power until it is spent

when: from 8:00 while grubs are alive, or your team just took grubs or Herald
asks: my jungler's top what do I do
they're doing grubs do I push
team's topside should I fight
nobody's bot am I safe
say: If your jungler's top for grubs, farm near your tower and skip trades, or take plates only when their jungler shows up top too.
more: When your team plays the other side, your lane's whole job is to give nothing back.
Their jungler has one useful answer to losing grubs: come to your lane. A pushed wave with no help invites a dive.
If he does show top, you have a short safe window to hit their tower.
check: Where your jungler and mid are, and whether their jungler has shown on the map.
breaks: If their jungler is missing and their mid has left lane, back off behind your tower even if it costs minions.
basis: pro:The lane without help gives nothing

when: after 20:00 with Baron alive and nobody on their team dead
asks: should we go baron
how do we set up baron
what do I do before baron
do I group for baron
say: Push the bot wave past river first, then group near Baron with your team, or just hold mid if you can't see their jungler.
more: Baron sits on the top side, so a bot wave pushing into their tower forces someone to leave or lose the tower.
Showing up at the pit with all three waves neutral lets them send five and fight you in a small space.
Don't be the one alone in bot when the fight starts. Shove, then leave straight away.
check: Where the three waves are, and how many enemies are visible.
breaks: If you are behind in items, do not start Baron at all. Push waves and wait for them to make a mistake.
basis: pro:Push the side waves before you posture at Baron

when: your gold is enough to finish an item and a dragon or Baron spawns in one to two minutes
asks: do I back before dragon
should I recall now or after
I have gold do I buy first
back or stay for the objective
say: Recall now so you're back with the item before it spawns, or stay only if one more wave gets you a bigger item.
more: Recalling a minute early means you arrive on time with the item. Recalling at the spawn means you arrive late or not at all.
A late recall right before a spawn is a numbers advantage you hand to the other team.
Push the wave before you go so it doesn't bleed into your tower while you shop.
check: How long until the spawn, and whether your wave is pushed out.
breaks: If the objective is already up and your team is on it, don't recall. Fight with what you have.
basis: pro:Before a spawn, arrive alive and on time

when: an ally died in the last 30 seconds and a dragon is up
asks: they're on dragon do I go
should I contest
we lost someone do we still fight for dragon
do I walk to river
say: Don't walk into river alone for this one; push bot and take tower damage instead, or go only if your whole team moves together.
more: A team already on the objective can stop hitting it and turn on whoever arrives one at a time.
Arriving late and alone usually costs more than the dragon: your life, a wave, sometimes another kill after.
Tower damage on the other side is something real to show for it.
check: How many enemies are at the pit, and whether your teammates are walking or still in base.
breaks: If it is their soul dragon, a late contest with your jungler is worth the risk. Stay behind him and hit from range.
basis: pro:Arrive together or do not arrive

asks: who do I hit
who should I focus
do I go for their carry
what's my target in fights
who do I shoot
say: Hit whoever is closest that you can reach safely, usually their tank, or switch to a carry only when they walk into your range.
more: Walking past their front line to reach a carry puts you in range of everything they have.
Steady damage on the nearest target wins long fights. The tank dies, and then nothing protects their back line.
If a carry steps forward to hit you, that is your moment. They came to you.
check: Who can reach you if you step forward, and which of their big abilities you saw used.
breaks: If their tank is far too tanky and their divers are already on you, hit the diver instead. Whoever threatens you comes first.

when: an enemy assassin has more kills than deaths
asks: their assassin keeps killing me
how do I fight with that assassin
I get one shot every fight
how do I not die instantly
say: Stand next to your support and let their assassin use everything first, or stay a screen back until he's shown on someone else.
more: An assassin needs you alone and in range before the fight starts. Take both away.
Once he has gone in on someone, he is the target. You get the rest of the fight for free.
Entering late costs a few seconds of damage, which is much less than being dead for the whole fight.
check: Where the assassin is right now, and whether your support is close enough to help.
breaks: If he is dead or showing in a side lane, play the fight normally from the start.

when: their team has an engage tank or an engage support
asks: how do I play against their engage
they keep jumping on me
where do I stand so I don't get caught
their tank keeps starting on me
say: Stay outside their engage range until it's used, then step up and shoot, or hit from max range and back off if it's still held.
more: Their engage is one big button. Before it is pressed you are the target, and after it you are the damage.
Don't stand next to your other carries. One engage should never catch two of you.
Keeping Flash for the engage, not for the chase, is what keeps you alive through it.
check: Whether their engage ability and Flash have been used, and where their tank is standing.
breaks: If your team has to start the fight, follow close behind your own tank instead of waiting, or they fight four against five.

when: your tank or engage teammate died in the last 15 seconds
asks: our tank died do I keep fighting
frontline's dead what do I do
should I run
do we still fight this
say: Your front line's gone, so back off toward your tower and clear the wave, or keep shooting only if they're lower than you and outnumbered.
more: With nobody in front of you, every one of their abilities is aimed at you next.
Leaving early keeps your death timer off the board, so the tower holds and the next fight is five against five.
The exception is a fight already won on numbers. Count living players before you turn.
check: How many are alive on each side, and how low the enemies near you are.
breaks: If you have no path out, fighting from under your tower is better than running in a straight line.

when: an enemy bruiser or juggernaut has the most kills on their team
asks: their top laner just runs at me
how do I deal with the fed bruiser
he dives me every fight
how do I kite him
say: Kite backward and shoot him as he walks at you, or leave the fight early if your team has nothing to slow him.
more: A bruiser wants a short fight on top of you. Every step he has to walk is free damage for you.
Fight near your own team so their slows and stuns land on him while he chases.
If he reaches you anyway, moving toward teammates beats moving toward open space.
check: Whether his gap-closer has been used, and which teammates near you can slow or stun.
breaks: If he ignores you and goes for another carry, stop running and shoot him. That is the fight you want.

when: a dragon is being fought over
asks: where do I stand at dragon
do I hit dragon or them
should I be hitting drake
where do I go in the dragon fight
say: Stand behind your tank on the side your team came from and hit whoever steps up, or turn to dragon only once they back off.
more: The pit is a small space. A carry inside it is easy to trap, so stay on the open side with a way out.
Your team needs one call: finish the dragon or fight. Splitting damage between the two does neither.
If they back off, your damage finishes the dragon fastest. If they come in, it should already be on them.
check: Whether the enemy is walking in or backing away, and where your exit path is.
breaks: If their jungler is close and the dragon is low, stop hitting it and zone him. A stolen dragon is worse than a slow one.
basis: pro:One call at an objective: finish it or fight

when: you are carrying Flash
asks: I have no flash how do I fight
flash is down can I still fight
no flash what do I do
I burned flash do we fight
say: Without Flash, shoot from max range behind two teammates and leave first, or skip this fight and farm a wave until it's back.
more: Flash is your answer to their engage. Without it, your position has to do that job.
Standing deeper costs some damage. Being caught costs all of it.
If the fight is optional, a couple of waves of farm while the cooldown ticks is a fine trade.
check: How long until your Flash is back, and whether an objective forces the fight now.
breaks: If it is a soul dragon or Baron fight, you have to be there. Stay at the very back and hit only what comes to you.

asks: do I follow them into the jungle
should I chase into their jungle
do I go in the brush
do I face check that
say: Fight in the open lane where you can kite, or wait at the exit of the choke rather than walking into a narrow path first.
more: Narrow jungle paths remove your range advantage. Everyone is in reach of everyone.
A carry should never be the first one into a dark brush. Let a tank or a ward go first.
Standing at the exit means they have to come out to you one at a time.
check: Whether the brush ahead is warded, and who on your team is in front of you.
breaks: If your team is already committed inside and winning, follow behind them. Being alone outside is worse.

asks: how do I teamfight as Jinx
what do I do in fights on Jinx
Jinx teamfight
where do I stand as Jinx
say: Shoot the front line until you get one takedown, then use the speed to chase, or drop chompers at your feet if they dive you.
more: Get Excited gives you a big burst of move speed and attack speed on a kill or assist. The first takedown is what turns the fight.
Until then you have no dash. Stay behind your team and be patient.
Flame Chompers root anyone who walks over them, so placed between you and a diver they buy time.
check: Who on their team can reach you, and whether their engage has been used.
breaks: If their divers are fed and your team can't hold them off, stay further back and use the rocket ult from range.

asks: how do I fight as Kog'Maw
Kog teamfight
what's my job in fights on Kog
where do I stand as Kog'Maw
say: Turn on your W and melt the nearest tank from behind your support, or back off entirely if their divers are still unseen.
more: Bio-Arcane Barrage gives you extra range and damage based on the target's max health, so tanks are good targets for you.
You have no dash at all. If someone reaches you, the fight is usually over for you.
Void Ooze slows whoever walks through it. Put it on the path between you and them.
check: Where their assassins and divers are, and how close your support is.
breaks: If nobody on your team can protect you this fight, poke with your ult from long range and don't walk up.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: how do I teamfight as Vayne
Vayne fights what do I do
who do I hit as Vayne
when do I go in on Vayne
say: Wait for the fight to start, then ult and work through their tanks from the side, or Condemn the first diver off you and reset.
more: Silver Bolts deal true damage based on max health every third hit, so you kill tanks faster than most marksmen.
Final Hour makes Tumble turn you invisible. Use that to dodge what's aimed at you, not to go deeper.
Your range is short, so going in first gets you killed. Second in is your spot.
check: Which of their stuns and roots have been used, and whether a wall is behind the diver for Condemn.
breaks: If they have several ranged threats that outrange you, stay with your team and only hit what comes forward.

asks: how do I teamfight as Caitlyn
Cait in fights
where do I put traps in a fight
what do I do as Caitlyn in teamfights
say: Put traps under your own feet and where they'll walk, then shoot from max range, or net away the moment someone reaches you.
more: A trap holds whoever steps on it and gives you an empowered Headshot, so a diver who lands on one is in trouble.
Your range is your safety. If you are close enough to be hit, you are too close.
The net knocks you backward. Aim it at the diver so it slows them and moves you away.
check: Where their divers are coming from, and whether your net is ready.
breaks: If the fight starts in an open area with no time for traps, skip them and just keep distance.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: how do I teamfight as Jhin
when do I ult as Jhin
Jhin fights
do I ult first or shoot
say: Channel your ult from far back once they're committed, or stay walking and shooting if someone can reach you during it.
more: Curtain Call fires four shots at extreme range, but you stand still while channeling. Only start it where nobody can get to you.
The shots stop on the first champion hit, so pick an angle where their tank isn't blocking the target you want.
Captive Audience traps slow anyone who walks over them. Put them on the path to you before the fight.
check: Whether any enemy can reach where you would channel, and who is standing in front of their carries.
breaks: If the fight is already on top of you, forget the ult and shoot the nearest target with your team.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: when do I use Ashe arrow
do I start fights with my ult
how do I teamfight as Ashe
Ashe arrow now or later
say: Fire your arrow at whoever steps up first to start the fight, or hold it for the diver if their assassin is still alive.
more: Enchanted Crystal Arrow stuns, and stuns longer the farther it flies. From range it is a real engage tool.
Your attacks slow, so once the fight starts nobody you are hitting gets away easily.
If something on their team can kill you alone, the arrow is your one defensive button. Don't open with it.
check: Whether your team is close enough to follow the arrow, and where their assassin is.
breaks: If your team is not in position, don't start with it. A stun nobody follows is a wasted ult.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: when do I go in as Samira
how do I teamfight Samira
Samira fights
do I dash in now
say: Wait until their stuns and roots are used on someone else, then dash in and ult, or shoot from range if they're holding them.
more: Inferno Trigger hits everyone around you, but you are standing in the middle of them. One stun ends it.
Blade Whirl destroys enemy missiles. Keep it for the one projectile that would stop you.
A kill refreshes Wild Rush, so the first kill gives you the dash to the next target or back out.
check: Which crowd control abilities you saw them use, and whether your team has already engaged.
breaks: If their crowd control can't be blocked or baited, play this fight as a normal marksman from the back.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: when do I ult as Miss Fortune
MF teamfight
how do I fight as MF
do I ult now
say: Hold your ult until your team locks them down, then fire it from a side angle, or use it early if they're stacked in a choke.
more: Bullet Time is a channel in a cone. Enemies held in place take all of it, and enemies who can walk out take little.
You stand still while it fires, so cast it from somewhere they can't immediately reach.
Make It Rain slows an area. It helps keep them inside the cone a little longer.
check: Whether your team has crowd control ready, and who on their team can interrupt you.
breaks: If their team has easy ways to interrupt a channel, use the ult only after those are spent.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: how do I teamfight as Xayah
when do I ult on Xayah
Xayah fights
what do I do in fights as Xayah
say: Shoot through the front line to lay feathers, then pull them back for the root, or save your ult to dodge their big engage.
more: Your attacks after an ability pass through targets and leave feathers. Bladecaller pulls them back and roots what they hit.
Featherstorm makes you untargetable for a moment. It is the best answer you have to a dive.
Feathers on the ground behind a diver mean he is rooted the moment he reaches you.
check: Where your feathers are lying, and whether their main engage has been used.
breaks: If you already used Featherstorm for damage, play much further back until it returns.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: how do I teamfight as Sivir
when do I use Sivir ult
what do I spell shield
Sivir fights
say: Keep your spell shield for their main engage ability and ult when your team goes in, or use the ult to run if it's lost.
more: Spell Shield blocks one ability. Pick the one that would get you killed and wait for it.
On The Hunt speeds up your whole team, so it works for starting a fight or escaping one.
Ricochet bounces between targets, so you deal damage to the group while hitting the tank in front.
check: Which enemy ability you most need to block, and whether your team is ready to go.
breaks: If their engage comes as several abilities at once, the shield only stops one. Stand further back instead.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: do I ult in as Kai'Sa
how do I teamfight Kai'Sa
Kai'Sa fights
should I dive their carry
say: Play front to back and hit what's close, or ult onto a carry only after their crowd control has been used.
more: Killer Instinct dashes you next to an enemy champion. That is deep in their team, and you need a way out.
Used late, the same ult cleans up a fight that is already won. Used early, it gets you killed.
Supercharge speeds you up, which helps you reposition after you land.
check: Which of their stuns you saw used, and how healthy the carry you want to jump on is.
breaks: If you are behind, don't use the ult to go in at all. Keep it to follow a teammate or to escape along the fight's edge.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: do I flank as Twitch
how do I teamfight as Twitch
Twitch fights
where do I come from as Twitch
say: Use Ambush and come from the side once they're fighting your tank, or stand behind your team and ult through them if flanks are warded.
more: Spray and Pray shoots bolts that pierce everything in a line. A side angle on a clumped team hits all of them.
Leaving Ambush gives you attack speed, so open from stealth right as the fight starts.
A flank only works unseen. If they have vision of you, you are a marksman alone on the wrong side.
check: Whether they have vision where you plan to come from, and whether your team is ready to start.
breaks: If your team needs you to hit the dragon or Baron, stay with them. A flank that arrives after the fight is worthless.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: how do I teamfight as Tristana
do I jump in as Trist
Tristana fights
when do I use Buster Shot
say: Shoot the nearest target and save Buster Shot to knock a diver away, or jump in only to finish someone when nobody can lock you down.
more: Your attack range grows as you level, so late in the game you can hit from further back than early on.
Buster Shot knocks its target back. Used on whoever jumps on you, it is a second escape.
Rocket Jump goes in or out. If you jump in, you have nothing left to leave with.
check: Which enemies can stun you after a jump, and whether Rocket Jump is ready.
breaks: If you need the kill to end the fight and it is one jump away, take it. Otherwise keep the jump for safety.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: how do I teamfight as Zeri
when do I ult on Zeri
Zeri fights
what do I do in fights as Zeri
say: Ult when several of them are close, then keep moving and shooting to build speed, or dash over a wall if they focus you.
more: Lightning Crash gives move speed that stacks each time you hit a champion. The longer the fight, the harder you are to catch.
Spark Surge carries you over terrain, so fighting near walls gives you an exit others don't have.
You want a long, moving fight. Don't trade your life for one burst of damage.
check: How many enemies are close enough for the ult to hit, and where the nearest wall is.
breaks: If they can burst you before the speed builds, start the fight from further back and let them come to you.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: when do I ult as Varus
how do I teamfight as Varus
Varus fights
do I start with my ult
say: Throw your ult at whoever walks up first so your team can collapse, or keep it for the diver that comes at you.
more: Chain of Corruption holds the first champion hit and spreads to others nearby. On a clumped team it can catch several.
Hail of Arrows slows and cuts healing on the ground it covers. Put it where the fight is happening.
A charged Piercing Arrow before the fight starts takes health off them for free.
check: Whether your team can follow up on the target, and where their divers are.
breaks: If the target is too far from your team to be followed, don't use it to start. Hold it defensively.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: how do I teamfight as Kalista
when do I ult my support
Kalista fights
what do I do in fights on Kalista
say: Hop between attacks and stack spears on the front line, or ult your support out if they get caught going in.
more: Every attack lets you lunge a short way. Keep moving and nobody without a hard gap-closer catches you.
Rend pulls out all the spears at once for damage and a slow. More spears first means a bigger hit.
Fate's Call brings your Oathsworn ally to you, and they can then dash back in and knock enemies back.
check: Where your support is, and whether they want to be pulled out or thrown back in.
breaks: If your support is not near the fight, the ult does nothing useful. Play it as a kiting fight.

when: you are level 6 or higher
asks: how do I teamfight as Nilah
when do I go in on Nilah
Nilah fights
do I dive as Nilah
say: Go in after your team engages and use your veil when their marksman turns on you, or wait outside if their mages are untouched.
more: Jubilant Veil dodges basic attacks, not spells. It is strong against auto-attackers and does little against mages.
Apotheosis pulls nearby enemies toward you, which lines them up for your team's area damage.
You fight at short range, so going in first means taking everything.
check: Whether their main damage comes from attacks or spells, and whether your team has started the fight.
breaks: If their damage is mostly spells, hang at the edge and only dash in to finish low targets.

asks: how do I teamfight as Ezreal
Ezreal fights what do I do
do I E in as Ezreal
what's my job as Ezreal
say: Poke with Mystic Shot before the fight starts and keep Arcane Shift to escape, or shift forward only to finish a lone low target.
more: Your damage comes from range before the fight, not from standing in it. A team that starts the fight hurt often loses it.
Landing Mystic Shot lowers your other cooldowns a little, so hitting it keeps your escape coming back.
